LLM auditresponse for .gitignore:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a standard gitignore configuration for an AUR package repository. It ignores all files by default (`*`), then explicitly un-ignores specific maintainer helper files: `.nvchecker.toml` (used for version checking automation), `.gitignore` itself, `PKGBUILD` (the package build recipe), and `.SRCINFO` (package metadata). This is a common and legitimate practice in AUR packages to ensure essential build files are tracked in version control while generated or temporary files are not. There are no security concerns with this configuration.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard gitignore configuration for AUR package files</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>
The file `.nvchecker.toml` is a configuration file for the nvchecker version-checking tool, used by the package maintainer to automate version checks for switchlet-bin. It contains standard, declarative fields: source set to "github", GitHub repository "jeppeklh/switchlet", use_latest_release enabled, and version prefix "v". The content consists solely of key-value pairs with no executable code, network requests, obfuscation, or dangerous commands. Even if the HTML entities (`"`) are interpreted literally, they represent inert data and cannot trigger malicious behavior. There is no evidence of supply chain attack, data exfiltration, or unauthorized system modifications.
</details>
